stage_b_review_note: Retains three fundamental-group descriptions on connected X: finite locally constant sets ↔ finite π1 sets; finite locally constant abelian sheaves ↔ finite π1 abelian modules; for finite Λ, finite-type locally constant Λ-modules ↔ finite π1 modules with commuting Λ action.

hypotheses: For a **connected** scheme $X$ with geometric basepoint $\bar x$, its étale fundamental group $\pi_1(X,\bar x)$ is the profinite automorphism group of the fibre functor of finite étale covers of $X$. A *finite continuous $\pi_1$-set* is a finite set with continuous action; a *finite continuous $\pi_1$-module* is a finite abelian group with compatible continuous action. A scheme is *geometrically unibranch* if every strictly henselian local ring has a unique minimal prime (equivalently the local geometric branches are unique); this is a hypothesis of the extension of the finite-type module correspondence to possibly infinite underlying fibre modules.
